Azure COVID-19 Data Engineering Pipeline

Introduction

This project implements an end-to-end data engineering pipeline on Azure to ingest, process, and report on COVID-19 data. It combines case, death, hospital admissions, and testing data published by the ECDC (European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control) with population reference data, producing clean, analysis-ready datasets and an interactive Power BI dashboard.

The goal was to build hands-on experience with a realistic, multi-stage Azure data pipeline — ingestion, transformation, governed storage, and reporting — mirroring the kind of architecture used in production data engineering environments.

Architecture

CI/CD: Pipeline artifacts (pipelines, datasets, data flows, linked services) are version-controlled through ADF's Git integration and deployed across Dev, Test, and Prod environments using ARM templates.

Technology Used

CategoryTools
OrchestrationAzure Data Factory
StorageAzure Data Lake Storage Gen2, Azure Blob Storage
TransformationADF Data Flows, Azure Databricks (PySpark)
DatabaseAzure SQL Database
ReportingPower BI
CI/CDGit, ARM Templates, Azure DevOps
SecurityService Principal, Azure Key Vault

Dataset Used

  • ECDC COVID-19 datasets (cases & deaths, hospital & ICU admissions, testing rates, country response measures) — publicly published by the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, ingested via HTTP connector
  • Population by age data — reference dataset (population_by_age.tsv.gz), sourced from Eurostat, loaded from Azure Blob Storage

Data Model

Transformed hospital admissions table, enriched with country and population lookups:

Scripts

Mounting Data Lake Storage in Databricks (Service Principal)

python
configs = {
    "fs.azure.account.auth.type": "OAuth",
    "fs.azure.account.oauth.provider.type": "org.apache.hadoop.fs.azurebfs.oauth2.ClientCredsTokenProvider",
    "fs.azure.account.oauth2.client.id": dbutils.secrets.get(scope="covid-kv", key="client-id"),
    "fs.azure.account.oauth2.client.secret": dbutils.secrets.get(scope="covid-kv", key="client-secret"),
    "fs.azure.account.oauth2.client.endpoint": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/oauth2/token"
}

dbutils.fs.mount(
    source="abfss://raw@covidstorage.dfs.core.windows.net/",
    mount_point="/mnt/covid-raw",
    extra_configs=configs
)

PySpark transformation — hospital admissions enrichment

python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("CovidHospitalAdmissions").getOrCreate()

# Read raw ECDC hospital admissions data from the mounted Data Lake path
raw_df = spark.read.csv("/mnt/covid-raw/hospital_admissions/", header=True, inferSchema=True)

# Reference lookup tables
country_lookup = spark.read.csv("/mnt/covid-raw/lookups/country_codes.csv", header=True, inferSchema=True)
population_lookup = spark.read.csv("/mnt/covid-raw/lookups/population.csv", header=True, inferSchema=True)

# Enrich raw data with country code and population lookups
enriched_df = raw_df \
    .join(country_lookup, raw_df.country == country_lookup.country_name, "left") \
    .join(population_lookup, "country_code_3_digit", "left") \
    .select(
        raw_df.country,
        country_lookup.country_code_2_digit,
        country_lookup.country_code_3_digit,
        population_lookup.population,
        col("year_week"),
        col("value").alias("hospital_occupancy_count")
    )

# Write curated output to Azure SQL Database
enriched_df.write \
    .format("jdbc") \
    .option("url", "jdbc:sqlserver://covidsqlserver.database.windows.net:1433;database=covid_db") \
    .option("dbtable", "dbo.transformed_hospital_admissions") \
    .option("user", dbutils.secrets.get(scope="covid-kv", key="sql-user")) \
    .option("password", dbutils.secrets.get(scope="covid-kv", key="sql-password")) \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .save()
